user_prompt: What is the effect of breastfeeding (direct breastfeeding or breast milk given during the procedure), compared with no intervention (routine care or no analgesic or comfort measure), on the duration of crying in seconds in term or preterm neonates undergoing a painful procedure (heel lance, venipuncture, intramuscular or intradermal injection, or similar)?  Effect measure: pool as a mean difference (MD) in seconds using a random-effects model. MD < 0 means less crying with breastfeeding (favours breastfeeding).  Outcome: duration of crying in seconds, extracted as the mean, SD and number of neonates per arm. - Use the total duration of crying during and immediately after the painful procedure (also called crying time or duration of first cry, as the paper defines it). If a paper reports several crying measures, prefer total crying time over latency to first cry, and do not use pain scores or percentages of time crying. - Convert minutes to seconds. Record the original unit and any conversion. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. If a paper reports only a median and range or interquartile range, estimate the mean and SD with a standard method and state it. - Control = no intervention (routine care, no analgesia, nothing given). Do not use another active control (sucrose, glucose, water, positioning, non-nutritive sucking, skin-to-skin contact without breastfeeding), for which the review has separate comparisons. - Multi-arm trials: when a paper compares breastfeeding, several other interventions and a no-intervention control, extract only the breastfeeding arm and the no-intervention arm. Read the column headings or group definitions carefully, because the no-intervention group may be listed first or last. If the same breastfeeding group appears in several comparisons, it can be used once here against the no-intervention group. - One row per trial; if a trial reports results separately for different procedures, use the primary procedure. - Include only randomised and quasi-randomised controlled trials in neonates (up to 28 days of age). Exclude studies in older infants and studies with no no-intervention arm.  Do not pool heart rate, oxygen saturation, pain scores such as PIPP or NIPS, crying measured as a percentage of time, or any other outcome.
